dataset: Musashi Book VII — The Perfect Light complete narrative scrape

evidence_policy.narrative_authority: All 16 local files under data/source/book7, read in full before web validation
evidence_policy.presence_rule: physically_present means on-page presence, including a directly narrated scene; letters, memories, reports, plans, distant prayers and names are mentioned_only
evidence_policy.coordinate_rule: No coordinates are emitted. Institutional confirmation of a locality never establishes an exact narrative point.
evidence_policy.web_scope: Geography and historicity only after local corpus freeze; external sources cannot add or override plot facts.

chapters.title: The Runaway Ox
chapters.end_summary: Otsū is safe with Sukekurō near Hannya; Toranosuke leaves after correcting the false warning; Ushinosuke's immediate return is not shown until the next chapter.

chapters.title: Hemp Seed
chapters.end_summary: Otsū is already traveling toward Edo; Gonnosuke and Iori leave Nara still seeking her; Hyōgo, Sukekurō and Ushinosuke remain associated with Koyagyū.

chapters.title: Sweepers and Salesmen
chapters.end_summary: Gonnosuke is a bound captive being taken toward the Mount Kudo network; Iori is alive in the ravine but separated, with his exact immediate route unknown.

chapters.title: A Pear Blossom
chapters.end_summary: Sado and Nuinosuke continue their journey; Gonnosuke remains captive at Kamuro under Daisuke and Benzō pending Yukimura's judgment.

chapters.title: The Port
chapters.end_summary: Iori is aboard Tatsumimaru under Sado's protection, bound for Kokura; Otsū has passed through Sakai without reuniting with him.

chapters.title: The Writing Teacher
chapters.end_summary: Gudō, Matahachi and Musashi are traveling west from Okazaki; Musashi has abandoned the Muka residence after his identity became exposed.

chapters.title: The Circle
chapters.end_summary: Gudō and Matahachi continue toward Kyoto; Musashi remains on the pass with a new insight, but his immediate destination is unstated.

chapters.title: Shikama Blue
chapters.end_summary: Otsū and Jōtarō are at the Mikazuki inn planning Himeji; Osugi is confined in the cave; surviving Hon'iden men are dispersed or wounded.

chapters.title: The Mercy of Kannon
chapters.end_summary: Otsū is unconscious but receiving aid; Osugi is remorseful and directing her own men to rescue Otsū; Jōtarō remains unaware at the inn.

chapters.title: The Tides of Life
chapters.end_summary: Musashi is sailing west; Gonnosuke and Kōetsu are in Osaka; Matahachi has gone after Akemi and her baby, with paternity unresolved.

chapters.title: The Evening Boat
chapters.end_summary: Otsū, Osugi and Jōtarō prepare to travel from Shikama toward Kokura; Musashi's ship continues west without a reunion.

chapters.title: A Falcon and a Woman
chapters.end_summary: Kojirō is at his Itatsu River house preparing for the Funashima duel; Omitsu and Kakubei contemplate marriage only after his return.

chapters.title: Before the Thirteenth Day
chapters.end_summary: Kojirō remains at his crowded house under intense pressure to win; Matahachi, Akemi and the baby are lodged in Kokura.

chapters.title: At Daybreak
chapters.end_summary: Musashi is at Tarōzaemon's Shimonoseki house planning an independent crossing; Sado and Iori prepare for Funashima; Matahachi and Akemi wait on a Kokura hill.

chapters.title: The Marriage
chapters.end_summary: Musashi and Sasuke are crossing toward Funashima; Otsū is acknowledged as Musashi's wife and remains on the Shimonoseki shore with Osugi, Gonnosuke and Jōtarō; Kojirō has already reached or is reaching the island.

chapters.title: The Soul of the Deep
chapters.end_summary: Kojirō is narratively dead on Funashima. Musashi leaves alive with Sasuke, but his destination and the conduct of Kojirō's supporters are unknown; Iori remains with Sado on the island.

events.description: Inshun visits Koyagyū and raises an alleged encroachment near Tsukigase while seeking Hyōgo's measure as a fighter.
Otsū leaves with Ushinosuke and the ox to see the blossoms without notifying the household.
Three rōnin threaten Otsū; Ushinosuke fights them, accidentally cuts the ox, and the animal bolts carrying Otsū.
Toranosuke stops the runaway ox and Sukekurō reaches Otsū near the Kasagi road.
Sukekurō recognizes Torazō as Hamada Toranosuke; Toranosuke explains the rōnin are expelled men, not Tōdō troops, and conceals himself because of Ono Tadaaki's disgrace.
After reading Takuan's old letter, Otsū insists on leaving for Edo the next morning and declines Hyōgo's escort.
Hyōgo tests Ushinosuke and accepts his request for training, using hemp-seed jumping to explain gradual skill.
Hyōgo rides toward Uji after news that Musashi's appointment was canceled, then turns back rather than impose the news on Otsū.
At the Kōfukuji field tournament Nankōbō defeats Daun and refuses the unidentified-looking mountain priest, later reconciled as Benzō.
Ushinosuke takes Iori's reed mat, defeats him near the pagoda, and the adults de-escalate; the boys reconcile through a potato contest.
Gonnosuke visits Kongōji through Oan and Tōroku and commissions a memorial service for his deceased mother.
Gonnosuke and Iori meet Kōetsu and Myōshū sweeping the temple grounds and discuss Musashi and the place's history.
The pursuing mountain priest attacks at a bridge; Iori strikes his eye with a stone and he retreats.
False cord merchants rig a log bridge and ambush Gonnosuke as an alleged Hōjō spy; Iori drops into the gully and Gonnosuke is bound.
Sado and Nuinosuke leave Mount Kōya; Daisuke invites them to Yukimura's Mount Kudo residence.
Sado and Yukimura discuss loyalty, Gudō, Musashi and the Hosokawa position while Sado remains wary of Osaka alignment.
Benzō arrives at Kamuro leading the bound Gonnosuke and calls him an Edo spy; Daisuke suppresses the accusation in Sado's presence.
The narrative explicitly identifies Rinshōbō, the mountain priest, as Toriumi Benzō, a leading Yukimura retainer.
Injured and separated from Gonnosuke, Iori meets Osei and Otsuru, descends to Kishiwada and crosses Osaka Bay with them.
Iori works at the Kobayashi establishment, fights Sahei over his sword and is tied outside as punishment.
Otsū walks past physically, but the gagged Iori cannot call effectively and she does not see him.
Months later Iori recognizes and attacks Kojirō; Kojirō orders a boiling-water punishment before Sado's arrival halts the danger.
Sado asks to take Iori to Kokura and train him as a samurai; Osei consents and Iori accepts.
Iori sails from Sakai aboard Tatsumimaru with the Hosokawa party for Kokura.
Under the name Muka, Musashi has spent about a year teaching writing in Okazaki's fishmongers' district.
Musashi meets Matahachi, who repents, urges him to marry Otsū and says his earlier coercion did not result in sexual contact.
Honda/Yoshioka-connected men ambush Musashi with muskets before dawn; he kills two and one escapes.
Watari Shima apologizes at the castle and Miyake Gumbei asks for instruction; Musashi demonstrates a two-weapons-as-one principle using muskets.
Gudō refuses Musashi's plea with 'not one thing' and walks west with Matahachi; Musashi follows toward Kyoto.
Musashi continues following Gudō and Matahachi through an austere stay at Daisenji and onward toward Hikone.
At a Lake Biwa temple Musashi reads Daitō Kokushi's testament while Gudō continues to deny him a conventional lesson.
On the pass Gudō draws a circle around Musashi and departs with Matahachi; Musashi moves from anger to insight about universe, self and sword.
Musashi stops pursuing; Gudō and Matahachi continue toward Kyoto while Musashi's next route is not specified.
Otsū works among Shikama dyers; Mambei falsely promises news through Musashi's sister and Jōtarō follows after recognizing her.
Mambei delivers Otsū to Osugi and Hon'iden men at Mikazuki shrine for payment.
Jōtarō kills Mambei, reveals himself as Aoki Jōtarō, confines Osugi in the cave and obtains her written instruction for the captors.
Jōtarō catches the captors, kills two and wounds others; Otsū frees herself and helps with stones before stopping pursuit.
Otsū and Jōtarō reunite and agree to go to his Aoki home in Himeji after discussing the rumor of a Kokura duel.
Otsū leaves the sleeping Jōtarō at the inn during the storm and returns alone toward the shrine.
Otsū frees Osugi from the cave despite Osugi's prior abduction attempt.
Osugi rejects Otsū's mercy, beats her unconscious, believes she has killed her and carries her into the cave.
An old maternal inscription forces Osugi to recognize her cruelty; she repents and tries to save Otsū.
A Hon'iden search party arrives and Osugi orders them to aid the unconscious Otsū.
In early fourth month 1612 Musashi boards a regular westbound ship from Sakai for the arranged duel at Kokura.
Gonnosuke arrives just after Musashi's vessel has left and learns that Iori is with Sado.
Gonnosuke reports that Yukimura recognized the error, freed him and apologized; he then searched neighboring provinces for Iori.
Gonnosuke elects to continue overland and walks with Kōetsu and Matahachi toward Osaka.
Matahachi sees Akemi with a baby, abandons his unfinished priestly path, returns the robe and goes after her intending to work and act as father; biological paternity is not established.
After Otsū's illness at Shippōji, Osugi nurses her, publicly cancels the old betrothal claim and remains transformed in conduct.
The party waits discreetly at Shikama while Himeji samurai prepare to contact Musashi's passing ship.
A samurai rows out and speaks with Musashi; he declines to disembark and the captain continues toward Kokura.
Otsū resolves to continue to Kokura despite illness, prepared even to receive Musashi's ashes.
Tadatoshi calls for a demonstration between Kojirō and Ujiie; both defer and the episode sharpens Kojirō's official standing and rivalry.
At Tadatoshi's order the challenge with Musashi proceeds under Hosokawa administration.
Kakubei reports that the council selected Funashima between Shimonoseki and Moji; Kojirō refuses to scout it.
Kakubei accepts the prospect of Kojirō marrying Omitsu after the duel; Omitsu remains anxious while Kojirō prepares through falconry.
Official notices announce the 13th-day, 8 a.m. Funashima bout and prohibit supporters and civilian vessels from the straits.
Matahachi and Akemi enter Kokura as a poor but functioning family unit while caring for the baby.
Gempachi reaches Kojirō's crowded house from Kōzuke and recounts Kojirō's lineage and training to the supporters.
Kojirō says he has written testaments for Kakubei and Omitsu and appoints Tatsunosuke and the falcon as his attendants for the crossing.
Kojirō's maternal aunt visits from Iwakuni, recalls raising him and gives an underrobe bearing supporters' protective inscriptions.
Musashi visits Sado's house, reunites with Iori and gives him grave counsel, but declines to stay and sends respects to Sado.
Six former Shimmen retainers invite Musashi to their annual horseshoe ceremony and simple feast, explaining their post-Sekigahara survival and Hosokawa service.
After fears that Musashi has vanished, Iori suggests Tarōzaemon's house; Nuinosuke and Iori find Musashi sleeping there.
Musashi refuses Sado's boat to avoid implying a factional challenge to Tadatoshi and confirms he will cross in Tarōzaemon's craft at his own time.
Nuinosuke reads Musashi's reassuring letter to Akemi and Matahachi, who then climb a hill to watch Funashima from afar.
Kojirō departs in Tadatoshi's new boat with Tatsunosuke and the falcon while Omitsu weeps unseen behind a tree.
During the crossing Kojirō releases the falcon and casts away the protective gifts and writings so he can face the fight without their burden.
Musashi delays preparations while completing two paintings, then dresses and leaves the house for Sasuke's hidden boat.
Osugi apologizes for her long persecution; Musashi forgives her and asks forgiveness for the trouble he caused since youth.
Musashi and Otsū reunite; when she asks to be called his wife for life, he silently nods and speaks of her as a samurai's wife and of himself as her husband.
Musashi boards Sasuke's boat; Otsū, restrained from running into the water, composes herself and bows with Jōtarō, Osugi and Gonnosuke.
On the tide-driven crossing Musashi carves a wooden sword from a broken oar and makes a paper tasuki.
Officials expel roughly forty unauthorized Kojirō supporters from Funashima to Hikojima, where they wait in armed boats for possible revenge.
Musashi lands at Funashima around ten, about two hours after the appointed time, while Kojirō and the witnesses wait.
Kojirō throws away his scabbard, cuts Musashi's headband with the Drying Pole, and is struck in the skull by Musashi's oar sword.
The narration states that Kojirō does not return to life; Musashi detects only a trace of breath before leaving and the book ultimately treats him as dead.
Musashi bows, returns to Sasuke's boat and leaves; the destination and any encounter with the armed supporters are explicitly unrecorded.

character_states.state: Alive after defeating Kojirō; departs Funashima with Sasuke. Destination and any clash with revenge parties are unrecorded.
Narratively dead after Musashi's blow. A trace of breath is detected before departure, but the narrator explicitly says he did not return to the living.
Alive on the Shimonoseki shore; acknowledged by Musashi as his wife and awaiting the duel's outcome.
Alive, reconciled with both Otsū and Musashi, bowing from the shore as Musashi departs.
Alive on the Shimonoseki shore after helping restrain and support Otsū; he missed speaking directly to Musashi.
Alive on the Shimonoseki shore after reuniting with Musashi and witnessing the farewells.
Alive on Funashima as Sado's attendant and witness to the duel.
Alive on Funashima, acting as senior witness and guardian of Iori.
Alive on Funashima, shocked by Kojirō's defeat but restrained by official duty.
Alive on Funashima as Kojirō's attendant; his post-duel disposition is not narrated.
Alive, taking Musashi away from Funashima by boat; destination unknown.
Alive with Akemi and the baby on a Kokura hill, watching and praying from afar; later movement is not shown.
Alive with Matahachi and her baby on a Kokura hill; biological paternity remains unstated.
Alive in Akemi's care on the Kokura hill.
Alive in Kokura after watching Kojirō depart; the planned marriage cannot occur after his narrated death.
Alive and based at Koyagyū, having accepted Ushinosuke as a pupil and stated an intention to serve the Owari Tokugawa in Nagoya.
Alive at the Yagyū orbit as Hyōgo's accepted pupil.
Alive, traveling under the Torazō concealment after rescuing Otsū; exact subsequent location unknown.
Alive, continuing toward Kyoto with Matahachi at the end of his direct appearance.
Alive in Osaka after accompanying Gonnosuke and receiving Matahachi's returned priestly garments.
